backlogged.summary: The F31 timeout tests that use a fake git shebang script return early on Windows (`if (!POSIX) return;`), so they pass without running there. The CI matrix includes windows, so kill-tree and timeout behaviour for git is unexercised on that platform. Consider `t.skip` or a .cmd fake so the skip is visible.

The git runners in lib/verify.mjs, lib/eval.mjs and lib/run.mjs each have their own timeout handling, and each calls gitTimeoutError separately. This duplication existed before F31, and F31 adds one more copy of the `r.timedOut` check in each. A single shared core git runner would remove it.

The `git config user.email` call in lib/commands/approve.mjs uses spawnSync without a timeout. It is a core git call outside the verify/eval/run paths that AC-1 names, so it is not covered by git_timeout_sec.
The eval repro commands still use step_timeout_sec. The SPEC §6 text describes them as user commands, so this is consistent, but the eval-phase timeout split is easy to misread.

validateUser accepts any finite positive budget.git_timeout_sec. Values above about 2147483.647 s (2^31-1 ms) overflow Node's setTimeout, which then fires after 1 ms, so every core git command would 'time out' at once. Consider an upper bound in validation. step_timeout_sec probably has the same issue.

Core git helpers now throw on timeout. When a git call in a cleanup path (for example verify's finally that runs `worktree remove --force` for the base worktree) times out, the new HarnessError(git) may replace the original error or result that was being reported. Previously a timed-out cleanup returned a result that the caller ignored.

Core git calls that run.mjs makes before the config is validated (before gitOpts.timeoutSec is set) use the default 300 s, not the configured budget.git_timeout_sec. This is harmless today because the ordering puts validation first, but gitOpts being mutated after the runners are created is an implicit invariant.
The POSIX-only fake-git tests (AC-1, AC-3, SC-1) return early on Windows and pass vacuously there, so the Windows taskkill /T path for core git timeouts has no end-to-end coverage.
